name: catalytic-crafting
target: WotLK 3.3.5a build 12340 / AzerothCore WotLK; Campaign Party bindings unknown
fantasy: A recipe is a small engineering choice: spend additional common materials for a larger batch, or insert a verified rare catalyst to choose a deterministic special output. Crafting remains server-authoritative and compatible with existing professions and Material Exchange.
non_negotiable_constraints: AzerothCore owns recipe admission, material consumption, output creation and ownership.
No addon-side output decisions; addons submit a recipe/catalyst intent only.
Do not replace profession learning, the existing Material Exchange, bags, inventory or AHBot.
Use existing client item displays, icons and spell visuals; no new art or model imports.
Every catalyst, output item, proc and enchant ID must be confirmed from local build-12340 data before use.
No surprise random destruction of rare catalysts; show exact cost and deterministic result before confirming.

upstream_source_snapshot.qualification: Source-path capability inspection only; not a Campaign Party pin, module compile, database test or runtime qualification.

core_mechanics.finding: Core validates fixed SpellInfo reagent IDs/counts and consumes them when the cast launches.
core_mechanics.design_effect: A dynamic optional catalyst is not a stock reagent toggle. It needs a server-side contract, a fixed recipe variant, or DBC-visible recipe variants.

core_mechanics.mechanic: crafted output amount and existing specialization logic
core_mechanics.finding: The core builds output from the effect quantity, clamps to stack size, then runs existing gem-perfection and profession-specialization extra-item logic before storing the item.
core_mechanics.design_effect: Deterministic batch-size boosts can build on the create-item path but must not double-apply or bypass existing specialization behavior.

core_mechanics.finding: SpellScript exposes OnCheckCast, OnCast, OnEffectHitTarget, PreventHitDefaultEffect, SetEffectValue and CreateItem helpers.
core_mechanics.design_effect: A module can validate a catalyst intent and select output behavior around an existing craft spell; exact hook timing and rollback must be verified in a compiled test module.

core_mechanics.finding: OnCast handlers run before core TakeReagents, and normal reagents are consumed before effect handling to free inventory space for crafted output.
core_mechanics.design_effect: Do not consume a rare catalyst blindly in OnCast. Inventory-full, interrupted, overridden or non-create outcomes need a reservation/commit/refund policy tested against actual core behavior.

core_mechanics.finding: The player create-item callback occurs after output storage succeeds, but its signature does not itself identify the recipe spell.
core_mechanics.design_effect: Choose/intercept the exact output before storage. The callback can confirm stored output and complete a receipt, but cannot safely choose/replace the item after the fact. A pending server-side craft context needs player + spell + cast/correlation identity and cleanup on all failure/timeout paths; do not infer recipe identity from the output item alone.

request.authority: Intent only. Server resolves the learned recipe, current profession skill, permitted character, catalyst definition and current inventory.
request.idempotency: One request_id may commit at most one output transaction; replays return the recorded result and never consume materials twice.

catalog_entry.extra_materials: Explicit item IDs and counts; may be one or more base materials or rare catalysts.
catalog_entry.output_rule: Exactly one of deterministic quantity increase, verified output variant, or verified existing enchant/proc application.
catalog_entry.fail_closed: Unknown recipe/material/output refs, missing evidence, collision, or unsupported item slot means reject without spending the optional catalyst.

augmentation_contract.compatibility_boundary: Campaign Party still chooses the active crafter and checks permissions; AzerothCore validates the spell/skill/materials and owns the resulting item. Material Exchange can provide deterministic material identities through an adapter, but its conversion rules remain downstream-owned.

design_patterns.player_choice: Use more common base materials for a deterministic larger batch.
design_patterns.example: A standard coat costs 8 bolts; a reinforced batch costs 16 bolts and yields 2 coats, subject to stack and inventory caps.
design_patterns.output: Same verified item identity and appearance; increase the create-item quantity only after cost and capacity checks.
design_patterns.risk: Must compose with built-in profession specialization extra-item behavior without multiplying twice.

design_patterns.player_choice: Insert a Moonstone catalyst to make a specific magical variant.
design_patterns.example: The same armor recipe plus 1 verified Moonstone yields a Moonlit variant with a verified stock frost/arcane proc or compatible enchant.
design_patterns.output: Prefer explicit variant item templates sharing a verified existing display; an instance enchant is possible only if its stock enchant is valid for that item slot and client.
design_patterns.risk: New variant item identities may need matching Item.dbc records; a new proc may need spell data and client parity.

design_patterns.player_choice: Use a region-specific reagent to give crafted goods a named, deterministic regional signature.
design_patterns.example: A crafting order using an approved Northrend reagent creates a different stock-spell effect or upgrade branch, while the base recipe remains craftable without it.
design_patterns.output: Campaign state and the server receipt record the branch; addon shows provenance only.
design_patterns.risk: Do not invent drops or rare IDs. Gather/quest supply must be balanced against the existing exchange and auction economy.

design_patterns.player_choice: Unlock new augment recipes through Cartographer or Relicwright progression without displacing a primary profession.
design_patterns.example: Discover a site, learn a catalyst formula, then ask a qualified existing crafter to produce the item.
design_patterns.output: Sidecar vocation gates discovery; AzerothCore still checks the actual crafting skill and item ownership.
design_patterns.risk: Requires durable server state and an explicit downstream adapter; does not become a true profession or replace Material Exchange.

recommended_first_slice.name: Moonlit Batch: deterministic quantity plus one catalyst variant
scope: one output variant reusing a verified item display
acceptance: Base recipe still works with its original reagent costs and output.
Batch augmentation consumes exactly the displayed extra base materials and yields a bounded deterministic quantity.
Catalyst augmentation consumes exactly one verified catalyst and produces only the selected server-authorized variant.
Missing catalyst, unknown output, invalid skill, permission denial, replayed request, inventory full, interruption and server restart never duplicate output or silently destroy the optional catalyst.
Existing specialization bonuses compose once, with a stated cap; normal and augmented craft paths are tested separately.
Clean-client tooltip, item appearance, proc/enchant, addon 3.3.5a UI and rollback all pass before release qualification.
recommended_first_slice.status: DESIGN_ONLY; no generator, module, SQL or gameplay implementation claimed

adjacent_ideas: Catalyst sockets as recipe choices, not permanently consumed item enhancements.
Cooperative party commissions where different selected characters contribute materials through an explicit Campaign Party escrow interface.
Recipe discovery as field research: clues unlock formulas, but the server remains the source of truth.
Supply-aware material rewards that feed existing Material Exchange identities and can be simulated against AHBot without taking over either authority.
One recipe, several deterministic schools: moonstone, ember, storm or void imprints, each mapped only to locally verified stock effects.
